name: microlog
listed_description: Extensible and configurable logging library with topics for embedded and desktop (awesome-c Utilities)
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. The README's 'Comparison with log.c' says only that a minimal configuration 'can match log.c's footprint in both size and performance' (directional, no numbers, and log.c is not faster-than-baseline evidence); doc/features.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and extensions/README.md contain no timing or size numbers; the repo has no benchmark directory (src, include, tests, example, extensions, doc only). No syslog or printf baseline is compared.

name: moderngpu
listed_description: moderngpu is a productivity library for general-purpose computing on GPUs. It is a header-only C++ library written for CUDA. The unique value of the library is in its accelerated primitives for solving irregularly parallel problems. (awesome-cpp Concurrency)
reason: No timing numbers against Thrust, CUB or another baseline in anything reachable: README, wiki pages Home, Introduction (compares only lines of code: cub 45,000, CUDPP 26,000, thrust 160,000 versus its 5,000), Release-notes and Load-balancing-search (says its lambda versions are slower than the hand-coded 1.0 kernels), tests/ and demo/ contain no benchmark or baseline timings. The moderngpu 1.0 'Performance' page lives on moderngpu.github.io, which is EGRESS_BLOCKED here (the wiki's raw Performance page is a 404). Search snippets say Merry's 'A Performance Comparison of Sort and Scan Libraries for GPUs' (arXiv 1601.03144) ranks Modern GPU second behind CUB for scan on a GTX 480, and that Thrust and MGPU have the fastest comparison-based GPU sorts, but arXiv, ar5iv and hgpu are blocked so no numbers were reachable; later segmented-sort papers report newer methods beating moderngpu. Retry the 1.0 performance page and the Merry paper from an environment that can reach github.io and arXiv.
